name: Shades Apart
label: Revelation
lede: A summer project from Bridgewater, New Jersey made its first record for $720, shot a Soft Cell cover for MTV in the bassist's backyard, and heard its major-label single on a Florida station right before Ricky Martin.

eras.title: Seven hundred and twenty dollars at Inner Ear
eras.text: Mark "V" Vecchiarelli, Kevin Lynch and Ed Brown started Shades Apart as a summer project in Bridgewater, New Jersey, listening to The Jam, The Police and The Clash as much as to hardcore. Their first record came out on Wishingwell, the label that had put out Youth of Today's Break Down the Walls.

years.h: Three friends start Shades Apart as a summer project in Bridgewater
years.p: Mark "V" Vecchiarelli plays guitar and sings, Kevin Lynch plays bass, Ed Brown plays drums. The same trio is still the band decades later.

years.h: Shades Apart record their debut at Inner Ear for $720
years.p: [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] and Eli Janney produce at Zientara's studio in Arlington, Virginia. Wishingwell Records releases it in December 1988.
years.xp:
Dave from Vision rode down for gang vocals, and the band treated the whole thing like a road trip. Lynch remembers grabbing burgers at a place in Arlington that turned out to be the original Five Guys.

They remixed it later at Trax East in South River, New Jersey, in a one-day Fourth of July session, with Mike "Wattage" Demko of TMA helping with guitar tones.

eras.title: College towns and day jobs
eras.text: Shades Apart slowed down while life happened: Ed Brown left for Virginia Tech and Mark Vecchiarelli became a father. When they came back, hardcore kids found them too melodic and college rock found them too loud, so they played college towns.

q: We always seemed to be somewhere in the middle of all that.
years.h: Neon arrives five years later, written around a Virginia Tech schedule
years.p: Drummer Ed Brown was at Virginia Tech while Shades Apart made their second record. Lynch says the band always sat somewhere between hardcore and indie.
years.xp: The Dude Danger EP also came out on Sunspot Records in this period. Mark Vecchiarelli had become a father in 1990.

eras.title: Descendents producers, a Soft Cell cover, MTV
eras.text: Revelation Records' Jordan Cooper knew Shades Apart from the Wishingwell days and signed them as the label widened past youth crew. With Descendents members producing, their cover of Tainted Love reached MTV.

years.h: Bill Stevenson produces Save It in South River, New Jersey
years.p: Descendents and [[ALL|e92547b5-a134-4149-af9a-c944af9e476f]] members [[Bill Stevenson|328e3ae5-7d8c-4a01-b2b3-b8f41fb7bb23]] and Stephen Egerton run the sessions at Trax East. Vecchiarelli says their energy in the studio never turned off, and it spread.
years.xp:
Ed Brown says Jordan Cooper knew the band from the Wishingwell era: Youth of Today had released Break Down the Walls on Wishingwell before Ray Cappo and Cooper started Revelation.

Revelation's first vinyl run was 3,012 black and 309 orange copies, after four black test pressings.

years.h: A Soft Cell cover shot in a backyard ends up on MTV
years.p: Shades Apart's Tainted Love, the Gloria Jones song Soft Cell made famous, gets MTV and MuchMusic play. The video was shot in Kevin Lynch's childhood backyard in Bridgewater.
years.xp:
Kevin Lynch says a young Benny Horowitz, later the drummer of [[The Gaslight Anthem|f208f09e-b5b3-4b06-87cd-f7230fae17e3]], is in the video somewhere.

On a MuchMusic appearance, the hosts were expecting Tainted Love and Shades Apart played a different song; the band figures the hosts were pretty mad. AllMusic calls it a surprise 1995 MTV hit.

years.h: Dinner on Sunset, next to the guitarist from Bush
years.p: On the Save It tour, Ed Brown remembers the band eating before a show on Sunset Boulevard, seated beside [[Bush|93ccd76c-3790-4435-a8bf-02bc26294b93]]'s guitarist.

years.cap: Seeing Things, recorded at the Blasting Room
years.h: Roofers rain shingle on the Seeing Things sessions
years.p: Shades Apart make Seeing Things (REV 57) with Jason Livermore at the Blasting Room in Fort Collins, Colorado, while a crew replaces the roof overhead.
years.xp:
Brown and Lynch slept in the guitar room. Between takes the band jumped off a cliff into Horsetooth Reservoir and got yelled at by a park ranger, someone caught crawdads in the stream by the studio, and Brown held push-up contests with Livermore, timed by an old Dr. Beat drum machine.

Lynch says there was no label pressure at all: they felt part of the family.

eras.title: Assholes and restaurants
eras.text: Universal Records signed Shades Apart and got them onto rock radio and the American Pie soundtrack. The label also sped up one of their songs without asking, then lost interest, and 9/11 closed the chapter.

years.h: Universal speeds up a Shades Apart song without asking
years.p: For Eyewitness the label wanted a radio-proven producer and got Lou Giordano over the Descendents crew. During mastering it sped up one song; the band rejected the change. An A&R man gave them that definition himself.
years.xp: The A&R man told the band that A&R was supposed to stand for Artists and Repertoire. Ron St. Germain mixed part of the record, and Ed Brown remembers watching Shark Week at Giordano's house while everyone else did real work.

years.h: Valentine reaches No. 31, then Ricky Martin takes over the radio
years.p: Valentine peaks at No. 31 on Billboard's Mainstream Rock chart. On a Florida radio tour, Kevin Lynch hears it on air, followed by Ricky Martin's Livin' la Vida Loca.

years.h: Vecchiarelli sits through American Pie waiting for the credits
years.p: Shades Apart's Stranger by the Day is on the film's soundtrack, and Mark Vecchiarelli watched it in a theater to catch the song.

years.big: "9/11 was kind of like the ending point."
years.p: Little marketing, less tour support, and a re-recorded Behind the Wheel from Seeing Things. Mark Vecchiarelli calls it the band's least favorite recording process.
years.xp: The label also picked a single Lynch didn't think was the right one. Ed Brown says the band was cooked by then, and Lynch says 9/11 became the point where they turned toward their families' future.

years.h: The 1995 cover turns up in She's Too Young
years.p: Shades Apart's Tainted Love is used in the 2004 film while the band is on hiatus.

eras.title: An album written by email
eras.text: Shades Apart never formally broke up, they just stopped. A few songs cut at the Blasting Room in 2011 turned, very slowly, into their first album in nearly twenty years.

years.h: A few songs at the Blasting Room, nine years on
years.p: Shades Apart return to Jason Livermore's studio in Fort Collins. Those sessions are the groundwork for their comeback album.

years.h: The same three, back on stage in 2012
years.p: Mark Vecchiarelli, Kevin Lynch and Ed Brown bring Shades Apart back to play shows, the same trio as 1988.

years.h: Revelation presses Save It again, in orange marble and blue
years.p: The vinyl run is 334 opaque orange marble and 766 blue copies.

years.h: Mike "Wattage" Demko dies a month before the comeback
years.p: The TMA guitarist who shaped the guitar sounds on Shades Apart's 1988 debut dies in July 2020, a month before Eternal Echo comes out.

years.src: No Echo · Punk Rock Theory · Salad Days
years.h: Eternal Echo arrives, nearly 20 years after Sonic Boom
years.p: Written by email, tracked separately, mixed by Jason Livermore and released by Hellminded Records of New Jersey. Lynch places it between Seeing Things and Eyewitness.
years.xp:
The spark was a friend's death: playing his tribute show, Lynch said, reminded them how fragile life is. Ed Brown wrote Souls and Soldiers after the 2017 Women's March in Washington (all three have daughters), and Only Light answers the August 2017 rally in Virginia.

Brown says none of them ever imagined making an album 35 years on.
